text: Long, long ago, in the land of Egypt, there lived a king called Pharaoh. He was very proud. He thought he was greater than everyone.
Pharaoh was cruel to one group of people, the Children of Israel. He made their lives very hard. And he gave a terrible order: their baby boys were to be taken away.
But Allah had a plan. Allah wanted to help the people who were being hurt, and one day to make them the leaders.
Who had a plan to help the people who were being hurt?
Allah
Pharaoh
Not Pharaoh. He was the one hurting them. Allah had a plan to help.
Find the pairs: things you can see in the land of Egypt.
In that hard time, a mother had a baby boy. His name was Musa. She loved him very much, and she was afraid the soldiers would find him.

Allah put a message in her heart: feed your baby. And when you are afraid for him, put him into the river. Do not be afraid, and do not be sad. We will bring him back to you, and make him one of the messengers.
She got a little chest ready, like a cradle. Tap to fit every piece.
With a brave heart, she laid baby Musa in the chest, and set it on the water of the great river.
Gently, gently, help the chest float out onto the river.
The river carried him along, gently, gently. And Allah was watching over baby Musa the whole way.
Tap each ripple to help the river carry him along.
What did Allah tell Musa's mother?
Hide and cry
Do not be afraid
No. Allah told her: do not be afraid, and do not be sad.
The river carried the chest right up to the palace of Pharaoh! The people of his house saw it in the water.
Pull the chest out of the water. Pull, pull, pull!
They carried it, still closed, to the queen. Her name was Asiya.
What is inside? Tap the chest to open it.
A beautiful baby boy!
Inside was a beautiful baby boy. And Allah filled her heart with love for him.
Everyone who saw baby Musa loved him. Tap every heart to make it glow.
Asiya said to Pharaoh: this baby will be a joy for me and for you. Do not harm him! He may help us one day, or we may take him as our son.
So baby Musa was safe, in the palace of the very king who was looking for baby boys. Pharaoh did not know what Allah had planned.
Who asked Pharaoh not to harm the baby?
Asiya, the queen
A soldier
No. It was Asiya, the queen. Allah had filled her heart with love.
At home, Musa's mother could think of nothing but her baby. Her heart felt empty. But Allah made her heart strong, so that she would keep on trusting Him.
She said to Musa's big sister: follow him. So his sister watched from far away, and nobody noticed her.
Follow the chest quietly along the bank. Tap each footprint.
In the palace, baby Musa was hungry. He cried and cried. Nurse after nurse came to feed him, but he would not drink from any of them.
Try every nurse. Tap each one. Baby Musa says no, no, no!
Then his sister stepped forward and said: shall I show you a family who will feed him, and take good care of him?
And who was it? Musa's own mother! He drank at once. Allah gave him back to her, so that her heart would be glad, and so that she would know: the promise of Allah is always true.
The queen even paid her to feed her own baby! It is told that only about a day and a night had gone by.
Who fed baby Musa in the end?
A palace nurse
His own mother
No. He would not drink from any nurse. Allah gave him back to his own mother.
What happened first? Tap them in order.
First, his mother put him on the river.
Then the queen found him and loved him.
Then he would not drink from any nurse.
And then he was back in his mother's arms.
Not that one yet. Think: what happened before it?
Musa grew up in the palace, like a prince. It is told that he even slept in the king's own room.
It is told that once, when he was little, Musa was given a sweet date and a hot, glowing coal. He put the coal to his tongue! After that, speaking was hard for him.
Help the little ones choose. Is it safe to eat, or too hot to touch?
Safe to eat
Too hot! Do not touch
A sweet date
A glowing coal
Warm bread
A candle flame
A cup of milk
Think again. Would it burn you?
When Musa was fully grown and strong, Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge. That is how Allah rewards the people who do good.
What did Allah give Musa when he was grown?
Wisdom and knowledge
A golden crown
Not a crown. Allah gave him wisdom and knowledge.
One day Musa walked into the city when the streets were quiet. He found two men fighting. One was from his own people. The other was from Pharaoh's people.
The man from his people shouted: help me! Musa hit the other man with his fist, just once. But the man fell down, and did not get up again.
Musa was so sorry. He said: this is the work of Shaytan. My Lord, I have done wrong. Please forgive me. And Allah forgave him. Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Kind.
Say sorry from the heart, like Musa. Press and hold the hands until they shine.
What did Musa do when he had done something wrong?
He pretended nothing happened
He asked Allah to forgive him
No. Musa said sorry straight away, and asked Allah to forgive him.
Soon the whole city knew what had happened. Then a man came running from the far side of the city. He said: Musa! The chiefs are coming to punish you. Leave now! I am giving you good advice.
So Musa left the city, afraid, looking over his shoulder. He prayed: my Lord, save me from the people who do wrong.
Help Musa slip away from the city.
Musa set off towards a land called Madyan. It was a long, long way. He said: I hope my Lord will guide me to the right way.
Walk with Musa across the desert. Tap each footprint.
At last he came to the water of Madyan. A crowd of shepherds were watering their sheep. And standing back, away from the crowd, were two young women, holding their sheep back.
Musa asked: what is the matter? They said: we cannot water our sheep until the shepherds have gone. And our father is a very old man.
It is told that a great heavy rock covered the well, a rock that it took ten men to lift. Musa lifted it all by himself!
Lift the heavy rock off the well. Pull, pull, pull!
Now give every sheep a drink. Tap each one.
When every sheep had drunk, Musa went to rest in the shade. He was tired and hungry, and far from home. He prayed: my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send me.
Musa had nothing left. Who did he ask for help?
Allah
The shepherds
No. Musa asked Allah: my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send me.
Find the pairs from the well of Madyan.
The two sisters went home and told their father what had happened. Soon one of them came back, walking shyly. She said: my father is asking for you. He wants to thank you for watering our sheep.
On the way, Musa walked in front. It is told that he asked her to walk behind him, and to throw a little pebble to show him which way to turn.
Show Musa the way. Tap where each pebble lands.
Musa told the old man his whole story. The old man said: do not be afraid. You are safe now.
One daughter said: father, hire him! The best person to hire is one who is strong, and can be trusted.
What makes the best helper?
Loud and bossy
Strong, and can be trusted
No. She said the best helper is strong, and can be trusted.
The old man said: I would like you to marry one of my daughters, and to work for me for eight years. Ten, if you choose. And Musa agreed.
It is told that Musa stayed the full ten years. Tap each sun to count them.
Musa was a shepherd now. Gather the sheep as they wander.
When his years of work were done, Musa set off on a journey with his family. One cold, dark night, he saw a fire, far away on the side of the mountain.
He said to his family: wait here. I can see a fire. Maybe I can bring you a burning stick to warm you, or find someone there to show us the way.
It is so dark. Slide your finger around to look, and find the fire.
Walk with Musa up to the fire.
When he came close, a voice called out: Musa! I am your Lord. Take off your sandals. You are in the holy valley of Tuwa.
Help Musa take off his sandals. Tap each one.
I have chosen you, so listen. I am Allah. There is no god but Me. So worship Me, and keep up the prayer, to remember Me.
Be very still and listen, like Musa. Press and hold the light.
Who called to Musa in the holy valley?
Allah, his Lord
A shepherd
No. It was Allah who called: Musa, I am your Lord.
Allah asked: what is that in your right hand, Musa? He said: it is my staff. I lean on it. I look after my sheep with it. And I use it for other things too.
Allah said: throw it down. Tap the staff to throw it.
It became a snake, moving fast! Musa turned to run. Allah said: pick it up, and do not be afraid. Tap the snake.
And it was a staff again.
The staff had become a real snake, and then a staff again. It was a sign from Allah.
Then Allah said: put your hand inside your shirt, and take it out. Tap the hand.
It shone white, bright and beautiful, and it did not hurt at all! Tap it again.
And it was just as before.
Musa's hand shone white. It is told that it shone like the moon. This was another sign.
Then Allah said: now go to Pharaoh. He has gone much too far.
Match each thing to what happened. Tap one on the left, then its partner on the right.
The staff
became a snake
The hand
shone white
The sandals
came off in the holy valley
Find the pairs from that wonderful night.
Musa was worried. He said: my Lord, I am afraid of what they may do to me. And speaking is hard for me. My brother Harun speaks better than I do.
So he prayed a beautiful prayer: my Lord, open up my heart. Make my task easy for me. And untie the knot in my tongue, so that they can understand my words.
And give me a helper from my family: Harun, my brother. Make me strong through him, and let him share my task, so that we may praise You and remember You a great deal.
Say Musa's prayer with him. Tap the parts in order.
My Lord, open up my heart.
Make my task easy for me.
Untie the knot in my tongue.
And give me my brother to help me.
Not yet. Listen again: heart, task, tongue, brother.
Allah said: Musa, you have been given what you asked for.
So Musa set off back to Egypt, with his brother Harun at his side.
Allah told them: go to Pharaoh, both of you. Speak to him gently, so that he may think, and remember. Do not be afraid. I am with you both. I hear and I see everything.
How should Musa and Harun speak to Pharaoh?
With shouting
Gently
No. Allah told them: speak to him gently.
Is it a gentle word, or a harsh word?
Gentle
Harsh
Please listen to me
You are stupid!
Let us talk together
Go away!
Peace be with you
Think again. How would it feel to hear that?
Musa and Harun stood before Pharaoh in his great hall. They said: we are messengers from your Lord. Let the Children of Israel go with us, and stop hurting them.
Musa showed them the clear signs that Allah had given him.
Which two signs did Allah give Musa? Tap them.
But Pharaoh and his chiefs said: this is nothing but magic tricks! We never heard of anything like this from our fathers.
Pharaoh said: have you come to push us out of our land with your magic, Musa? We will bring you magic just like it. So choose a day!
Musa said: let it be the day of the festival. And let all the people gather when the sun is high.
Which day did Musa choose?
The day of the festival, with everyone watching
A secret night, with nobody there
No. Musa chose the festival day, so that everyone could see the truth.
Help gather all the people for the big day. Tap them as they come.
The big day came. The sun was high, and the whole city was there. Pharaoh's magicians stood in a row, with their ropes and their sticks.
Musa warned them: do not make up lies about Allah! Then they said: Musa, will you throw first, or shall we? Musa said: you throw.
Who threw first?
Musa
The magicians
No. Musa said to the magicians: you throw first.
They threw down their ropes and their sticks. And by their magic, the ropes seemed to wriggle and slither, just like snakes!
Look closely. They are only ropes! Tap each one to see what it really is.
Even Musa felt afraid inside. But Allah said: do not be afraid. You will win. Throw down what is in your right hand.
Throw down the staff! Tap it.
It swallowed up everything the magicians had made!
Musa's staff swallowed up everything they had made, every rope and every stick, until nothing was left.
Help the staff swallow the tricks. Tap the ropes as they appear.
The magicians knew magic, and they knew this was no trick. They fell to the ground and said: we believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa!
Why did the magicians believe?
They saw it was no trick. It was from Allah
Pharaoh told them to
No. Pharaoh was furious! They believed because they saw it was truly from Allah.
Pharaoh was furious. He shouted: how dare you believe before I say you may? And he said he would punish them terribly.

But the magicians were not afraid any more. They said: we will never choose you over the clear signs that have come to us. Do what you like. You only rule this short life. Allah is better, and Allah lasts for ever.
What did the magicians choose?
Pharaoh's gold
The truth from Allah
No. They gave up Pharaoh's rewards. They chose the truth from Allah.
There was a man in Pharaoh's own family who had kept his faith a secret. He spoke up: would you hurt a man only because he says, my Lord is Allah? He has brought you clear signs!
And Asiya the queen believed too. She prayed: my Lord, build me a house near You in the Garden. And save me from Pharaoh, and from what he does.
Make her prayer with her. Press and hold the hands until they shine.
But proud Pharaoh said to his chiefs: I know of no god for you but me! Haman, bake bricks of clay, and build me a tall tower, so that I can climb up and look for the God of Musa. I think he is lying.
Pharaoh thought a tower could reach the sky. Tap to stack the bricks and see.
Up and up it went. But no tower can reach Allah. Pharaoh and his armies were proud in the land, with no right to be.
Who said it? Match the brave hearts to their words.
The magicians
We believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa
Asiya the queen
Build me a house near You in the Garden
The secret believer
My Lord is Allah
Still Pharaoh would not let the people go. So Allah sent signs to Pharaoh's people, to wake them up. First came years with no rain, and hardly any food grew.
Then came a great flood of rain. It is told that it spoiled the crops and the fruit.
Then came clouds of locusts that ate up the plants. It is told that they even chewed the nails out of the doors!
Shoo! Tap the locusts to chase them off the plants.
Then tiny bugs got into the grain. And then came frogs. Frogs, frogs, everywhere! It is told that they were in the pots, in the beds, and even in the clothes.
Find every frog hiding in the kitchen. Tap them all.
And then the water of the river turned red. Every one of these was a clear sign.
Each time, they begged: Musa, pray to your Lord for us! If the trouble goes away, we will believe, and we will let your people go. Musa prayed, and Allah took the trouble away.
Musa prays, and the trouble is lifted. Rub the sky until it is clear.
But every time the trouble was gone, they broke their promise.
What did they do each time the trouble went away?
They broke their promise
They kept their promise
No. Every time, they broke their promise.
Five signs came, one after another. Tap them in order.
First, the flood.
Then the locusts.
Then the tiny bugs.
Then the frogs.
And then the red water.
Not that one yet. Rain, locusts, bugs, frogs, red water.
At last, Allah told Musa: leave by night, with My servants.
Quietly wake the families. Tap each house to light its lamp.
Quietly, quietly, in the dark, the families took what they could carry, and followed Musa out of Egypt.
Lead the people out of Egypt.
When Pharaoh found out, he was furious. He gathered a huge army and chased after them. At sunrise, he caught up.
In front of the people was the sea. Behind them was Pharaoh's army. The people cried: we are caught!
But Musa said: no! My Lord is with me. He will guide me.
What did Musa say when everyone was afraid?
We are lost
My Lord is with me
No. Musa said: my Lord is with me. He will guide me.
Allah told Musa: strike the sea with your staff.
Strike the sea! Press the staff and hold, and watch.
And the sea split in two! Each side stood up like a huge mountain, with a dry path in between.
It is told that there were twelve paths, one for each of the twelve families, with windows in the water so that they could see each other. And Allah sent the wind to dry the ground.
Help the wind dry the path. Rub away the water.
Count the twelve paths. Tap each one.
Walk the people across, between the walls of water.
Musa and all his people crossed safely to the other side.
Pharaoh and his army rushed in after them. Then the sea came crashing back together, and the army was gone.
As the water closed over him, Pharaoh cried: I believe in the God that the Children of Israel believe in! But it was too late.
All his life he had been proud and cruel. Allah saved only his body, as a sign for the people who came after.
The people were free! That day is called Ashura. Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, told the Muslims to fast on that day.
Who saved Musa and his people?
Allah
A big boat
No, there was no boat. Allah opened the sea for them.
Tell the story of the sea. Tap in order.
First, they were caught between the sea and the army.
Then Musa struck the sea with his staff.
Then a dry path opened, and everyone crossed.
And then the sea closed again.
Not that one yet. What came before it?
Now the people travelled through the hot, dry desert. And Allah sent clouds to give them shade.
Allah sent down food for them too: a special food called manna, and little birds called quails. Eat from the good things We have given you!
Gather the manna in your basket. Tap each piece.
Here come the quails! Tap each little bird.
Then the people were thirsty, and there was no water anywhere. Musa prayed for water. Allah said: strike the rock with your staff.
Strike the rock! Tap it twelve times, and count the springs.
Twelve springs came gushing out of the rock, one for each of the twelve families. And everybody knew their own place to drink.
How many springs came out of the rock?
Two
Twelve
No. Twelve springs, one for each of the twelve families.
Find the pairs: the gifts Allah sent in the desert.
Allah called Musa to the mountain for thirty nights, and then ten more. Musa said to his brother Harun: take my place with my people, and do what is right.
Thirty nights, and ten more. How many nights is that?
Forty
Thirteen
Count again. Thirty and ten make forty.
Climb the mountain with Musa.
On the mountain, Allah spoke to Musa. Musa said: my Lord, let me see You. Allah said: you will not see Me. But look at that mountain. If it stays in its place, then you will see Me.
Then Allah showed His glory to the mountain, and the mountain crumbled into dust! Musa fell down in a faint.
What happened to the mountain?
It grew taller
It crumbled into dust
No. The mountain could not stay in its place. It crumbled into dust.
When he woke up, Musa said: glory be to You! I turn back to You, and I am the first to believe.
Allah said: Musa, I have chosen you, with My messages and My words. So hold on to what I give you, and be thankful. And Allah gave him the Tablets, with guidance for his people.
Musa was told: be thankful. Is it thankful, or not thankful?
Thankful
Not thankful
Saying: thank You, Allah
Saying: I want more, more, more
Sharing your food
Throwing good food away
Think again. Would a thankful person do that?
While Musa was away on the mountain, a man called the Samiri played a wicked trick. The people threw their gold jewellery into the fire, and out of it he made the shape of a calf.
The golden calf made a sound like a cow. It is told that this was only the wind blowing through it. The Samiri said: this is your god! And many of the people believed him.
But the calf could not talk to them. It could not guide them. It could not help them, or hurt them, at all.
Could the golden calf hear them, or help them?
No. It was only gold
Yes, it could
No. It could not speak, or guide, or help. It was only a thing made of gold.
Who is it true about? Only Allah, or the golden calf?
Only Allah
The golden calf
Made the earth and the sky
Was made by a man's hands
Hears every prayer
Cannot say a single word
Gives us our food and water
Think again. A statue cannot do anything.
Harun told them: my people, this is only a test for you! Your Lord is the Lord of Mercy. Follow me! But they said: we will not stop until Musa comes back.

Musa came back, angry and very sad. He put down the Tablets, and took hold of his brother. Harun said: son of my mother, the people would not listen to me! Then Musa prayed: my Lord, forgive me and my brother.
Musa sent the Samiri away. And the calf was ground into dust, and scattered into the sea.
Grind the calf into dust and blow it away. Rub, rub, rub!
The people were sorry for what they had done. And Musa told them: your God is only Allah. There is no god but Him.
What happened first? Tap them in order.
First, the gold went into the fire.
Then the Samiri made the calf.
Then Musa came back, angry and sad.
And then the calf was dust in the sea.
Not that one yet. What came before it?
One day Musa told his people: Allah commands you to sacrifice a cow. They said: are you joking with us?
Instead of doing as they were told, they asked: what kind of cow? Musa said: not too old, and not too young, but in between. Now do as you are told!
But they asked again: what colour? Musa said: a bright yellow cow, lovely to look at.
And they asked again: which one exactly? Musa said: a perfect cow, with no marks on it at all, one that has never pulled a plough or watered the fields.
Find the right cow: bright yellow, with no marks at all. Tap it.
At last they found it, and did as they were told. But they very nearly did not! And Allah used it to bring out a truth that some of them had been hiding.
What should they have done at the start?
Asked more and more questions
Done as they were told, straight away
No. All those questions only made it harder. They should have obeyed straight away.
They asked three questions. Tap them in order.
First they asked: what kind of cow?
Then they asked: what colour?
And then they asked: which one exactly?
Not that one yet. Kind, then colour, then which one.
Musa said: my people, remember the gifts Allah has given you. Go into the holy land that Allah has promised to you, and do not turn back.
But they said: Musa, there are strong, frightening people in that land. We will not go in until they have left!
Two men who trusted Allah said: go in through the gate! If you go in, you will win. Put your trust in Allah.
What did the two brave men say?
Trust Allah, and go in
Run away and hide
No. The two men said: go in through the gate, and put your trust in Allah.
But the people said: you and your Lord go and fight. We are staying right here.
Musa said: my Lord, I can only answer for myself and my brother. And Allah said: then that land is closed to them for forty years. They will wander in the desert.
Round and round they wandered. Tap each footprint.
Is it brave trust, or a fearful excuse?
Brave trust
Fearful excuse
Go in through the gate!
We are staying right here
Put your trust in Allah
You go. We will wait
Think again. Is that trusting Allah?

One day, someone asked Musa: who knows the most, of all the people? Musa said: I do. So Allah told him: there is a servant of Mine, at the place where the two seas meet, who knows things that you do not know.
Musa said to his young helper, Yusha: I will not stop until I reach the place where the two seas meet, even if it takes me years! They took a fish with them in a basket.
Travel with Musa and Yusha to where the two seas meet.
They stopped to rest by a rock. And there, the fish slipped out of the basket, into the sea, and swam away! It is told that the water stood over its path like a little tunnel.
Follow the fish along its path through the water. Tap each splash.

They walked on and on. Musa said: bring us our lunch. This journey has made us tired. Then Yusha remembered: the fish! By the rock, it went off into the sea, in such a strange way. Shaytan made me forget to tell you.
Musa said: that is the very place we were looking for! So they turned around, and followed their own footsteps all the way back.
Follow the footsteps back to the rock. Tap each one.
And there they found a servant of Allah, to whom Allah had given mercy and special knowledge. It is told that his name was al-Khidr.
Musa asked: may I follow you, so that you can teach me? He said: you will not be able to be patient with me.
Musa said: if Allah wills, you will find me patient. He said: then do not ask me about anything, until I tell you about it myself.
What did Musa promise al-Khidr?
To ask lots of questions
To be patient, and not to ask
No. Musa promised to be patient, and not to ask about anything.
They got into a boat. It is told that the sailors knew al-Khidr, and took them for free. And then al-Khidr made a hole in the boat!
Musa cried: do you want the people in it to sink? Al-Khidr said: did I not tell you that you could not be patient with me? Musa said: forgive me. I forgot.

A little bird landed on the edge of the boat, and dipped its beak in the sea. Al-Khidr said: my knowledge and your knowledge, next to the knowledge of Allah, are like the sip this bird took from the sea.
How much is all that we know, next to what Allah knows?
Like one little sip from the sea
Like the whole sea
No. It is only like the sip of a little bird, from the whole sea.

Then came something much harder for Musa to understand. It was about a boy, and it is a story for when you are older. Musa spoke up again. Then he said: if I ask you about anything after this, send me away.

They came to a town and asked for food, but nobody would give them any. In that town was a wall that was about to fall down. And al-Khidr fixed it! Musa said: you could have asked them to pay you for that.
Help mend the wall. Tap to put every brick back.
Al-Khidr said: this is where you and I must part. But first, I will tell you what it all meant.
The boat belonged to poor people who worked on the sea. A king was coming who took every good boat by force. So I made it look damaged, and he would leave it alone.

And the wall belonged to two orphan boys. Hidden under it was a treasure, kept for them. Their father had been a good man. Allah wanted them to grow up, and find it for themselves. I did none of this by my own choice.
The treasure is safe under the wall. Brush away the sand to see it.
Match each strange thing to its secret.
A hole in the boat
kept it safe from a greedy king
A mended wall
kept a treasure safe for two orphans
Musa learned that Allah knows what we do not know. Sometimes a thing looks bad, and there is good hidden inside it.
Our Prophet, peace be upon him, said: we wish Musa had been patient, so that Allah would have told us more about the two of them.
What did Musa learn?
That he knew everything
Allah knows what we do not know
No. Musa learned that Allah knows what we do not know.
What a story! A baby on the river. A boy in the palace. A shepherd by the well. And then a prophet, who stood before a king with only a staff in his hand.
And every step of the way, Allah was with Musa, hearing and seeing everything.
Allah gave Musa the Book, to be a light, and a guide, and a mercy for the people.
Tell the whole story of Musa. Tap in order.
First, a baby on the river.
Then a shepherd at the well.
Then the fire on the mountain.
Then the sea opened.
And then the Tablets, on the mountain.
Not that one yet. What came before it?
Who is who? Match each person to their part.
Asiya
the queen who loved baby Musa
Musa's sister
followed the chest along the river
Harun
the brother who helped him speak
Pharaoh
the proud king, lost in the sea
One last game. Find all the pairs from the story of Musa.
This is the story of Musa, peace be upon him. When the sea was in front of him, and the army was behind him, he said: my Lord is with me. He will guide me.
